Where required by the fire code official, address identification shall be provided in additional approved locations to facilitate emergency response.[§R319.1] 2). There shall be a landing or floor on each side of each exterior door. The width of each landing shall be not less than the door served. Landings shall have a dimension of not less than 36 inches measured in the direction of travel. The slope at exterior landings shall not exceed 1/4 unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2 percent). [§R311.3] 3). Landings or finished floors at the required egress door shall be not more than 1-1/2 inches lower than the top of the threshold. [§R311.3.1] 4). Doors other than the required egress door shall be provided with landings or floors not more than 7-3/4 inches below the top of the threshold. [§R311.3.2] 5). Penetrations of wall or floor-ceiling assemblies required to be fire-resistance rated in accordance with Section R302.2 (through penetrations) or R302.3 (membrane penetrations) shall be protected in accordance with this section. [R§302.4]. 6). Membrane penetrations shall comply with Section R302.4.1. Where walls are required to have a fire-resistance rating, recessed fixtures shall be installed so that the required fire-resistance rating will not be reduced. [§R302.4.2] 7). Smoke alarms or smoke detectors shall be installed a minimum of 20 feet horizontal distance from a permanently installed cooking appliance, unless allowed by exception. [§314.3.3]

corrections: SB 9 application required Due on 04/08/2024 , assigned to Katrina Lapira Marked as Corrections on 04/08/2024 by Katrina Lapira Due on TBD , assigned to Katrina Lapira Marked as Review Needed on 05/24/2024 by Shanitra Roan Comment: Reset due to resubmittal Due on 06/17/2024 , assigned to Katrina Lapira Marked as Corrections on 06/17/2024 by Katrina Lapira Due on TBD , assigned to Katrina Lapira Marked as Review Needed on 08/27/2024 by Autumn Maltbie Comment: Reset due to resubmittal Due on 09/18/2024 , assigned to Katrina Lapira Marked as Approved w/Conditions on 09/23/2024 by Katrina Lapira Comment: Redline onto plans the following condition of approval: Specific Tree Preservation Requirements (on page 6 of the report) will be met and reported on. These requirements include - The consulting arborist must review all plans to adequately assess impacts to trees. These include, but are not limited to, improvement plans, utility and drainage plans, grading plans, landscape and irrigation plans and demolition plans. Protect the root zone that will remain undisturbed (the area outside the building foundation/ retaining walls/ flatwork) will be critical to the survival of tree #500. Install a sturdy, metal fence around tree #500. The goal would be to enclose as much if the root zone surrounding the tree as possible, while allowing the demolition, rough grading and building construction. When it is time to construct the concrete path and/ or the deck, the fencing would be temporarily moved and replaced following each phase on the construction. Minimize any grading of the area around tree #500 to the greatest extent possible Design the deck surrounding tree #500 to have the fewest piers possible and to keep piers as far from the tree as possible. Additional support and/ or use the metal beams may allow the deck to span greater distances between piers. Design the opening in the deck that will surround the trunk of the tree #500 to provide a min of 6" between the deck materials and the tree. Consider a design that will allow the deck material to be easily removed in sections to accommodate future growth of the tree trunk. The species has been known to exceed several feet in diameter. Conditional Approval - Action Required: Be sure to upload the completed Construction Waste Management Plan (form #172) with a valid Green Halo tracking # into the permit service center portal. Without it the project may be delayed when you set an appointment for final inspection. Online link to the form is located here: https://berkeleyca.gov/construction-development/permits-design-parameters/permit-types/permit-forms Construction Waste Management form completion is solely the responsibility of project owners, property managers, or contractors only. Architects and designers are not required to complete this form. The property owner, project manager, or contractor can initiate the Green Halo Project. Once the Green Halo project is operational, City of Berkeley staff can reassign it to the property owner, project manager, or contractor at any time, enabling them to upload valid weight tickets from approved facilities. However, this form with the Green Halo tracking # is required prior to issuance in the portal for Zero Waste’s final approval. The Zero Waste Division offers in-person office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Permit Service Center, situated at 1947 Center Street, third floor with existing City of Berkeley Green Halo projects. Should you require assistance prior to initiating your Green Halo project, contact RecyclingProgram@berkeleyca.gov via email.

State code (CALGreen) requires a minimum of 65% of the waste generated by construction and demolition activities must be diverted away from landfill disposal through any combination of recycling, salvage, reuse or composting. The City of Berkeley also requires 100% diversion of asphalt, concrete, and land clearing debris must be recycled and/or salvaged for reuse. As a residential structure that is increasing the building’s condition area, volume, and/or size, this project is required to divert construction and demolition waste and debris from landfill disposal. Please provide a completed Construction Waste Management form. [CGBSC 301.3.2 and BMC 19.37.040]. Be sure to upload the completed Construction Waste Management Plan (form #172) with a valid Green Halo tracking # into the permit service center portal. Without it the project may be delayed when you set an appointment for final inspection. Online link to the form is located here: https://berkeleyca.gov/construction-development/permits-design-parameters/permit-types/permit-forms. Construction Waste Management form completion is solely the responsibility of project owners, property managers, or contractors only. Architects and designers are not required to complete this form. The property owner, project manager, or contractor can initiate the Green Halo Project. Once the Green Halo project is operational, City of Berkeley staff can reassign it to the property owner, project manager, or contractor at any time, enabling them to upload valid weight tickets from approved facilities. However, this form with the Green Halo tracking # is required prior to issuance in the portal for Zero Waste’s final approval. Please submit a Construction Waste Management Plan via Green Halo at www.berkeley.wastetracking.com. Prior to permit final, weight tickets for all materials disposed and recycled must be uploaded. Photos are acceptable for salvaged/reused materials. The Zero Waste Division offers in-person office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Permit Service Center, situated at 1947 Center Street, third floor with existing City of Berkeley Green Halo projects. Should you require assistance prior to initiating your Green Halo project, contact RecyclingProgram@berkeleyca.gov via email.

Be sure to upload the completed Construction Waste Management Plan (form #172) with a valid Green Halo tracking number and permit number into the permit service center portal. Without it the project may be delayed when you set an appointment for final inspection. Online link to the form is located here: https://berkeleyca.gov/construction-development/permits-design-parameters/permit-types/permit-forms Construction Waste Management form completion is solely the responsibility of project owners, property managers, or contractors only. Architects and designers are not required to complete this form. The property owner, project manager, or contractor can initiate the Green Halo Project. Once the Green Halo project is operational, City of Berkeley staff can reassign it to the property owner, project manager, or contractor at any time, enabling them to upload valid weight tickets from approved facilities. However, this form with the Green Halo tracking # is required prior to issuance in the portal for Zero Waste’s final approval. The Zero Waste Division offers in-person office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Permit Service Center, situated at 1947 Center Street, third floor with existing City of Berkeley Green Halo projects. Should you require assistance prior to initiating your Green Halo project, contact RecyclingProgram@berkeleyca.gov via email.

Be sure to upload the completed Construction Waste Management Plan Form #172 with a valid Green Halo tracking number (GHXXX-XXXX-XXX) and permit number (B20XX-XXXXX) into the permit service center portal. Without it the project may be delayed when you set an appointment for final inspection. Online link to the form is located here: https://berkeleyca.gov/construction-development/permits-design-parameters/permit-types/permit-forms. Construction Waste Management form completion is solely the responsibility of project owners, property managers, or contractors only. Architects and designers are not required to complete this form. The property owner, project manager, or contractor can initiate the Green Halo Project. Once the Green Halo project is operational, City of Berkeley staff can reassign it to the property owner, project manager, or contractor at any time, enabling them to upload valid weight tickets from approved facilities. However, this form with the Green Halo tracking # is required prior to issuance in the portal for Zero Waste’s final approval. If the project type is Demolition/Deconstruction, New Construction, Remodel, Repair/Reconstruction, or Tenant Improvement, you will require a unique Green Halo tracking number and submit a Construction Waste Management form for each project type/permit application, regardless of if the project address is the same. Please note that you may only use one permit number when creating a Green Halo project. Additionally, please refrain from combining or using other permit numbers on your Green Halo application, as this practice may delay the review process. The Zero Waste Division offers in-person office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Permit Service Center, situated at 1947 Center Street, third floor with existing City of Berkeley Green Halo projects. Should you require assistance prior to initiating your Green Halo project, contact RecyclingProgram@berkeleyca.gov via email.

1.) APPROVED - Berkeley Fire Department - Fire Prevention Division Field Inspection NOT Required. 2.) Smoke and Carbon monoxide alarms: Ensure smoke and carbon monoxide alarm are installed in accordance with CRC §R314 and §R315. 2.1.) Smoke alarms installed greater than 10-ft but less than 20-ft horizontal distance from a permanently installed cooking appliance must be an ionization smoke alarm with an alarm-silencing switch or photoelectric smoke alarm. [CRC §R314.3.3 (NFPA 72 §29.8.3.4 Item 4)] 2.2.) Smoke alarms installed greater than 6-ft but less than 10-ft horizontal distance from a permanently installed cooking appliance must be a photoelectric smoke alarm. [CRC §R314.3.3 (NFPA 72 §29.8.3.4 Item 4)] 2.3.) Smoke alarms must be installed not less than a 3-ft horizontal distance from the door or opening of a bathroom that contains a bathtub or shower. [CRC §R314.3.3 (NFPA 72 §29.8.3.4 Item 5)]. 2.4.) Smoke alarms shall not be installed within 36-inches horizontal path from the supply registers of a forced air heating or cooling system and shall be installed outside of the direct airflow from those registers. [CRC §R314.3.3 (NFPA 72 §29.8.3.4 Item 5)]. 2.5) Smoke alarms and combination smoke/carbon monoxide alarm must be interconnected. [CRC §R314.4 and §R315.5] 2.6.) Smoke alarms must be listed in accordance with UL 217 and State Fire Marshal approve for smoke alarms. 2.7.) Combination smoke/smoke carbon monoxide alarms listed in accordance with UL 2034 and UL 217 and State Fire Marshal approve for smoke alarm. [CRC §R315.4]

Green Halo Requirements: State code (CALGreen) requires a minimum of 65% of the waste generated by construction and demolition activities must be diverted away from landfill disposal through any combination of recycling, salvage, reuse or composting. The City of Berkeley also requires 100% diversion of asphalt, concrete, and land clearing debris must be recycled and/or salvaged for reuse. As a new residential structure valued over $100,000, this project is required to divert construction and demolition waste and debris from landfill disposal. Please provide a completed Construction Waste Management form. [CGBSC 301.3.2 and BMC 19.37.040] Be sure to upload the completed Construction Waste Management Plan (form #172) with a valid Green Halo tracking # into the permit service center portal. Without it the project may be delayed when you set an appointment for final inspection. Online link to the form is located here: https://berkeleyca.gov/construction-development/permits-design-parameters/permit-types/permit-forms. Construction Waste Management form completion is solely the responsibility of project owners, property managers, or contractors only. Architects and designers are not required to complete this form. The property owner, project manager, or contractor can initiate the Green Halo Project. Once the Green Halo project is operational, City of Berkeley staff can reassign it to the property owner, project manager, or contractor at any time, enabling them to upload valid weight tickets from approved facilities. However, this form with the Green Halo tracking # and permit application # are both required prior to issuance in the portal for Zero Waste’s final approval. Please submit a Construction Waste Management Plan via Green Halo at www.berkeley.wastetracking.com. Prior to permit final, weight tickets for all materials disposed and recycled must be uploaded. Photos are acceptable for salvaged/reused materials. The Zero Waste Division offers in-person office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Permit Service Center, situated at 1947 Center Street, third floor with existing City of Berkeley Green Halo projects. Should you require assistance prior to initiating your Green Halo project, contact RecyclingProgram@berkeleyca.gov via email. Waste Collection Requirements: 1. City of Berkeley Residential Accounts: a. In accordance with California State Law SB 1383, BMC 12.35.010, BMC 12.32.030 all residential accounts must subscribe to weekly garbage/refuse, compost, and recycling services. b. In accordance with California State Law SB 1383 all residential accounts must sort garbage/refuse, compostable, and recyclable materials into the appropriate containers. c. Residential customers with 1-4 units must contact the City of Berkeley’s Customer Service at least four weeks prior to the anticipated service start date for refuse/garbage and compost service at (510) 981-7270 or customerservice@berkeleyca.gov. d. State code (CALGreen) requires a minimum of 65% of the waste generated by construction and demolition activities must be diverted away from landfill disposal through any combination of recycling, salvage, reuse or composting. The City of Berkeley also requires 100% diversion of asphalt, concrete, and land clearing debris must be recycled and/or salvaged for reuse. As a new residential structure valued over $100,000, this project is required to divert construction and demolition waste and debris from landfill disposal. Please provide a completed Construction Waste Management form. [CGBSC 301.3.2 and BMC 19.37.040]. Be sure to upload the completed Construction Waste Management Plan (form #172) with a valid Green Halo tracking # into the permit service center portal. Without it the project may be delayed when you set an appointment for final inspection. Online link to the form is located here: https://berkeleyca.gov/construction-development/permits-design-parameters/permit-types/permit-forms. Construction Waste Management form completion is solely the responsibility of project owners, property managers, or contractors only. Architects and designers are not required to complete this form. The property owner, project manager, or contractor can initiate the Green Halo Project. Once the Green Halo project is operational, City of Berkeley staff can reassign it to the property owner, project manager, or contractor at any time, enabling them to upload valid weight tickets from approved facilities. However, this form with the Green Halo tracking # is required prior to issuance in the portal for Zero Waste’s final approval. Please submit a Construction Waste Management Plan via Green Halo at www.berkeley.wastetracking.com. Prior to permit final, weight tickets for all materials disposed and recycled must be uploaded. Photos are acceptable for salvaged/reused materials. The Zero Waste Division offers in-person office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Permit Service Center, situated at 1947 Center Street, third floor with existing City of Berkeley Green Halo projects. Should you require assistance prior to initiating your Green Halo project, contact RecyclingProgram@berkeleyca.gov via email. Be sure to upload the completed Construction Waste Management Plan Form #172 with a valid Green Halo tracking number (GHXXX-XXX-XXXX) and permit number (B20XX-XXXXX) into the permit service center portal. Without it the project may be delayed when you set an appointment for final inspection. Online link to the form is located here: https://berkeleyca.gov/construction-development/permits-design-parameters/permit-types/permit-forms. Construction Waste Management form completion is solely the responsibility of project owners, property managers, or contractors only. Architects and designers are not required to complete this form. The property owner, project manager, or contractor can initiate the Green Halo Project. Once the Green Halo project is operational, City of Berkeley staff can reassign it to the property owner, project manager, or contractor at any time, enabling them to upload valid weight tickets from approved facilities. However, this form with the Green Halo tracking # is required prior to issuance in the portal for Zero Waste’s final approval. If the project type is Demolition/Deconstruction, New Construction, Remodel, Repair/Reconstruction, or Tenant Improvement, you will require a unique Green Halo tracking number and submit a Construction Waste Management form for each project type/permit application, regardless of if the project address is the same. Please note that you may only use one permit number when creating a Green Halo project. Additionally, please refrain from combining or using other permit numbers on your Green Halo application, as this practice may delay the review process. The Zero Waste Division offers in-person office hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Permit Service Center, situated at 1947 Center Street, third floor with existing City of Berkeley Green Halo projects. Should you require assistance prior to initiating your Green Halo project, contact RecyclingProgram@berkeleyca.gov via email.
